title: Antonio Rudiger accuses Getafe defender of ‘exaggerating’ ’10-game ban’ challenge
content:
Antonio Rudiger says Getafe’s Diego Rico “exaggerated” after the Real Madrid defender was accused of risking inflicting serious damage to the Getafe full-back during their La Liga fixture.

Rudiger, 33, admitted the challenge looks “terrible” when replayed in slow-motion but insisted it was not intentional, adding had he purposely wanted to do Rico harm “he (Rico) wouldn’t have gotten up”.

The Germany international caught Rico in the face with his knee while the Getafe player was on the floor during the first half of the league game at the Bernabeu on March 2, before catching him again in the face with his shin as he fell to the ground. Rico accused Rudiger of attempting to “smash my face in” and said the challenge could have received a “10-game” ban.

“It looks terrible if you see it in slow motion,” Rudiger told a press conference on Monday. “Since the player said I almost killed him, I don’t think he needed to say that because if I had wanted to, he wouldn’t have gotten up.

“I don’t take anything away from it, but as the player said that it was almost that I killed him or something like this. I don’t think he needs to exaggerate, I don’t justify it but the way he spoke after the game it was like I killed him and he was running after.

“Sometimes the VAR replays look awful, but it was never my intention to do this. I have limits, and I’m a human being. I think the guy exaggerated a bit; maybe he wants to be the star. We see what happens in the world.”

Rudiger’s challenge went unpunished as it was not spotted by referee Alejandro Muniz Ruiz and the video assistant referee (VAR) did not recommend an on-field review. Spain’s refereeing committee (CTA) later confirmed the VAR should have intervened and recommended Rudiger be dismissed for violent conduct.

“If it had been the other way round, I might have been given a 10-game suspension and I wouldn’t have played for the rest of the season,” Rico told radio station Cadena Cope. “I don’t know what the VAR is there for — I think it’s there for these situations.

“(It’s) an attack, you know he’s going to hit me on purpose. Because in the previous play, we have a scuffle where the referee whistles for a foul and as he’s (Rudiger’s) going back to defence he starts saying things and in the very next play, the ball comes to me and you see how he almost moves his team-mate away to smash my face in. If he’d got me badly, he could have left me there directly on the pitch.”

Rico completed the full 90 minutes at the Bernabeu, with Getafe winning 1-0.
